newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE may be knocked down to 4,330-4,340.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE may be knocked down to 4,330-4,340.

text.p: The 4,350 level on the FTSE 100 index -- so critical to defend if the market stands any chance of a near-term advance -- will be lost by the close on Wednesday, technical analysts said.
Negative sentiment will knock the FTSE back down to the 4,330-4,340 region today and its powers of recovery from there will be slim, they added.
And it is now likely to stay below its 25-day moving average, which is currently at 4,362 and which has been a reasonably good supporting trendline since December.
By 0821 GMT, the FTSE was indicated down 10.0 at 4,346.8.
By Tuesday, the FTSE had retraced 61 percent of the gains it made -- on an intra-day basis -- between the low of 4,287.3 on March 3 and its high of 4,466.3 on March 11.
A full two-thirds retracement would indicate a target of 4,347 but the current weak sentiment could mean an overshoot of that target, analysts said.

Any meaningful recovery by the FTSE today will depend on today's consumer price index data for February from the U.S. which economists are forecasting to have risen by 0.2 percent and the core rate, which excludes food and energy, to also be up by 0.2 percent.
Figures significantly higher than these will heighten expectations of a rise in U.S. interest rates next week and will depress U.S. and UK equities, analysts said.

If these inflation figures come in line with forecasts, it should bring temporary relief to the equities but there will still be a worry about whether the Federal Reserve will raise U.S. rates as a pre-emptive move following recent data showing a robust U.S. economy, they added.
